- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.33) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% of recent mean or spike magnitude.
- After a price spike (≥ 2% from prior 5-day avg), model often over-estimates continuation; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.25) and price is falling, model frequently under-anticipates drop; add 0.5–1.5% downward bias to forecast.
- Model shows strong mean-reversion bias in early 30d horizon; if forecast is > 1.5σ above recent 10-day mean, reduce by 0.5–1.0σ.
- When sentiment is flat (0.00) and price is trending, model often fails to capture momentum; add 0.3–0.7% lagged momentum adjustment.
- For 30d horizon, model consistently under-forecasts late-period (days 25–30) prices; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias for final 5 days if sentiment is neutral or positive.
